headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risks from shared Dify datastore and Khoj indexed notes; no critical compliance issue is evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dify can ingest uploaded knowledge-base files and uses shared state via the Dify server datastore, while Khoj indexes personal notes/documents and can search them. That creates a plausible path where attacker-controlled content in one system is surfaced to the other as trusted text. The bridge is documented, but not a raw shared channel, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Dify ingests content originating from Khoj-indexed notes without provenance labels, injection risk is present.
IF Khoj returns retrieved text that Dify later treats as instructions, the pathway is active.
mitigations: Add provenance tags to retrieved snippets before passing them between systems.
Disable automatic instruction-following on retrieved text in Dify workflows.
Restrict shared datastore access to read-only for retrieval outputs.
Manually review cross-system content before execution.
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware filtering between retrieval and agent prompts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents read filesystem-backed content and touch sensitive classes: Dify handles knowledge-base content and conversation logs, while Khoj handles personal notes and indexed documents. Because Dify also has broad network egress and can call model providers, sensitive content from a shared or copied workspace could leave the local boundary. The profiles show a plausible default path, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF the same documents are indexed in Khoj and uploaded into Dify, both systems will process the same sensitive corpus.
IF Dify forwards conversation or knowledge-base content to external model providers, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Separate sensitive and non-sensitive corpora before indexing or upload.
Turn off or narrow Dify model-provider access for sensitive workflows.
Use distinct storage locations for each agent.
Review retention settings for logs and indexed documents.
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters on outbound prompts.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dify can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; Khoj can read the filesystem but cannot write it. The profiles do not show overlapping write access or shared mutable resources, so direct capability conflict is limited. A conflict could still arise if both are pointed at the same writable directory, but that is not established here.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same directory, file clobbering becomes possible.
IF an operator grants Khoj write access outside the profile, the conflict assessment changes.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Keep Khoj read-only for shared content.
Avoid concurrent writes from Dify workflows.
Snapshot files before running Dify jobs.
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared mutable workspace.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dify is an orchestration platform that can wire tools into agent or workflow apps, while Khoj is a retrieval system that returns notes and documents. If Dify consumes Khoj output as authoritative context, errors or hallucinations in retrieval can cascade into downstream actions. The pair lacks a built-in verification step in the profiles, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Dify uses Khoj retrieval results as direct prompt context, cascading error is active.
IF Dify workflows take actions based on retrieved text without human review, downstream impact increases.
mitigations: Insert a verification step before any action-taking workflow.
Require citations or source links for retrieved claims.
Limit Dify actions to draft-only mode.
Review high-impact outputs manually.
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds and source validation gates.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and self-hostable, and the evidence does not show a residency, certification, or retention mismatch. Dify touches conversation logs and knowledge-base content; Khoj touches personal notes and indexed documents, but no specific regulatory conflict is documented. Because the other agent is not implicated in a distinct compliance boundary, low is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF one deployment stores regulated data in Dify while the other stores it in a different jurisdiction or retention regime, compliance risk increases.
IF either agent is configured with external cloud processing for regulated data, the assessment changes.
mitigations: Keep regulated data in one controlled deployment.
Align retention settings across both systems.
Document data flows for each corpus.
Use self-hosted modes for sensitive data.
requires-engineering: implement jurisdiction-aware routing and retention enforcement.
